text:
anya: Quick question — we keep talking about tenant isolation but I want to be explicit: do we want implicit tenant affinity (derived from API key) or require an explicit X-Org-ID header for all internal calls?
liam: leaning toward implicit for ease of use, but worried about background jobs and operator proxies where affinity can change.
sasha: implicit is nice for UX, but it hides origin. harder to reason about when keys get reused across teams. audit trails suffer.
anya: right. proposal: primary surface is tenant-anchored API keys (implicit), but add a required actor header when performing cross-tenant ops or impersonation. header could be X-Rdwd-Actor: svc:billing@org-123
liam: +1 if we enforce header for any proxy/bridge paths. how do we make enforcement practical? config per route?
sasha: per-route enforcement in the gateway makes sense. gateway knows whether route allows cross-tenant. default deny if header present but key tenant != target tenant.
devx: UX cap: devs will forget headers. suggest a warning metric and a linter rule in SDKs that fails local tests when using cross-tenant routes without explicit actor header.
anya: good call. also need to think about ephemeral tokens for background workers. worker should exchange long-lived key for ephemeral scoped token with explicit claims.
liam: that exchange sounds similar to our existing token-broker pattern but tighter: broker mints a token with claims {org, actor, ttl, purpose}. crucial to include "purpose" string for auditing.
sasha: audit: store both originating API key id and minted ephemeral token id. chain of custody = [api_key_id -> token_id]. we should store that in request logs (sampling for high volume).
security-bot: note: add telemetry ticket https://rwd/board/telemetry-452 for chain-of-custody fields (api_key, actor, token_id, route).
anya: edge case: operator proxy that needs to act on behalf of customer A but runs in org B. We must forbid implicit affinity here. require explicit attestation signed by operator KMS.
liam: attestation flow idea: operator generates signed blob {target_org, actor, ttl, nonce} and we validate via public key. returns 403 if signature missing/invalid.
sasha: downside: complexity & ops for customer-managed KMS. tradeoff: accept operator-managed attestation for certain trusted partners only (enterprise opt-in).
devx: SDK note: we'll provide helpers for attestation signing in node/python and an integration guide. make it an enterprise feature flag.
anya: final ask: can someone write a short RFC follow-up that captures: - implicit tenant API keys as default - explicit X-Rdwd-Actor for impersonation/cross-tenant - gateway per-route enforcement - token-broker for ephemeral tokens with purpose claim - attestation for operator proxies (enterprise opt-in) - audit fields & sampling plan
liam: I'll draft it. ping me if you want specific examples.
sasha: happy to review. also add migration checklist for services that currently infer tenant from headers/hosts.
anya: thanks all :thumbsup:
